It is commonly called '''Murayama Tenjin'''. {{nihongo|'''Tenman Shrine (Takayama)'''|天満神社 (高山市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Hida Province]].

== Outline and history ==
The founding year is unknown. When the army of {{ill|Anejikōji Tadamori|Q56346475|qid=Q56346475}}, a mid-ranking {{ill|Kuge|Q1196276|qid=Q1196276}} and military leader in the {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}}, was defeated in battle, an image of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ar|سوغاوارا نو ميتشيزانه|br|Sugawara no Michizane|ckb|سوگاوارا نۆ میچیزانێ|de|Sugawara no Michizane|es|Sugawara no Michizane|fa|سوگاوارا نو میچی‌زانه|fi|Sugawara no Michizane|fr|Sugawara no Michizane|id|Sugawara no Michizane|it|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真|kk|Сугавара но Митидзане|ko|스가와라노 미치자네|la|Sugawara no Michizane|ms|Sugawara no Michizane|nl|Sugawara no Michizane|nn|Sugawara no Michizane|pl|Michizane Sugawara|pt|Sugawara no Michizane|ru|Сугавара-но Митидзанэ|sh|Sugawara no Michizane|sv|Sugawara no Michizane|th|สึกาวาระ โนะ มิจิซาเนะ|tr|Sugawara no Michizane|uk|Суґавара но Мітідзане|zh|菅原道真|zh_classical|菅原道真|zh_min_nan|Sugawara no Mitizane|qid=Q382005}} handed down in his family was enshrined here, and since then the shrine has drawn worship as Tenjingū, deity of learning. However, it is also said that earlier, Hida no Kuni no Miyatsuko Ōyatsuki-no-Mikoto first enshrined Amatsukami here, and thus it came to be a joint enshrinement with Amatsukami. It is also recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} as a {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}} for the shikinaisha {{ill|Ōtsu Shrine (Hida)|Q11437362|qid=Q11437362|lt=Ōtsu Shrine}} (with a possible scribal confusion of Ōtsu/Tsu).

On the {{ill|Fluvial terrace|Q1069618|qid=Q1069618}} around the shrine is the buried-cultural-property site “Murayama ruins.” In the {{ill|keidai|Q11429002|qid=Q11429002}} is a “Jōmon pit-dwelling site,” remains of a {{ill|Indicator (genus)|Q1087793|qid=Q1087793}}, designated a Gifu Prefecture {{ill|Historic site|Q1081138|qid=Q1081138}}<ref name="縄文式住居跡">{{Cite web|和書|date=2015-10-15|url=https://www.pref.gifu.lg.jp/page/7296.html|title=Jōmon pit-dwelling remains |publisher=Gifu Prefecture |accessdate=2022-10-19}}</ref>.

Under the name “Jōmon pit-dwelling remains,” it was designated a prefectural {{ill|Historic site|Q1081138|qid=Q1081138}} on February 24, {{ill|1956|Q5221|qid=Q5221}} (Shōwa 31)<ref name="縄文式住居跡"/>.
